title: Voice of Customer  Empathy Grid
subtitle: You're writing marketing copy, designing a feature, or preparing a sales pitch but you're
useWhen: writing from your perspective, not your customer's. Your message is accurate but it doesn't land.
howToUse: The Empathy Grid, popularised by IDEO and widely used in design thinking, maps what your customer Thinks and Feels, Sees, Hears, Says and Does, and their Pains and Gains. Combined with Voice of Customer (VOC) research - the actual words customers use to describe their problems - it builds a rich picture of the customer's inner world. AI can simulate this map quickly when given enough context, and help you extract VOC language from customer interviews or reviews. A grid built from assumptions just formalizes your own guesses. VOC matters because customers rarely describe problems the way you'd describe your solution.
steps: Feed AI your customer's industry, role, and the problem they face. 2. Also paste in any real customer reviews, interview notes, or support tickets you have.
Focus especially on the Pains and Gains quadrants, these drive copy and product decisions.

Pull exact phrases from the VOC output and use them verbatim in your marketing. Get inside your customer's head before building or writing anything AI can simulate an empathy map but it cannot replace real customer conversations. Use the AI output as a hypothesis - then verify at least three points directly with an actual customer before writing copy or making product decisions
origin: IDEO Design Thinking — Empathy Map, popularised early 2000s
promptBody:
PROMPT — COPY & PASTE READY
Act as a customer research analyst using the Empathy Grid.
Customer profile  :  [ROLE, INDUSTRY, COMPANY SIZE]
Problem context   :  [WHAT CHALLENGE THEY FACE DAILY]
Real customer data (if available):
[PASTE REVIEWS, INTERVIEW NOTES, OR SUPPORT TICKETS]
Map the full Empathy Grid:
THINKS & FEELS  :  Inner concerns, hopes, and worries
SEES                       :  What their environment looks like
HEARS                    :  What colleagues, managers, media tell them
SAYS & DOES        :  Public behaviour and statements
PAINS                     :  Frustrations, fears, obstacles
GAINS                     :  Desired outcomes and measures of success
After the grid: give me 5 exact phrases this customer would use to describe their
problem in their own words, not marketing language.
